business_studies.title: Nature and Significance of Management
objectives: Describe the characteristics of management and its importance in an organisation.
Explain the nature of management as an art, science and profession.
Explain the functions of management.
Appreciate the nature and importance of coordination.
business_studies.summary: Management coordinates resources to achieve organisational goals efficiently and effectively. The outline covers its nature, objectives, importance, levels and functions, and explains why coordination connects the work of different parts of an organisation.

business_studies.title: Principles of Management
objectives: State the meaning, nature and significance of principles of management.
Explain Taylor’s principles and techniques of Scientific Management.
Explain Fayol’s principles of management.
business_studies.summary: Management principles offer general guidance for decisions and actions. This outline considers their significance alongside Fayol’s principles and Taylor’s scientific management, including its principles and techniques and the comparison between their contributions.

business_studies.title: Business Environment
objectives: Explain the meaning of business environment.
Discuss the importance of business environment.
Describe the various elements of business environment.
business_studies.summary: The business environment consists of external forces that affect organisations. Its importance and economic, social, technological, political and legal dimensions provide a framework for understanding how businesses respond to changing conditions.

business_studies.title: Planning
objectives: State the meaning of planning.
Describe the features and importance of planning.
Explain the limitations of planning.
Analyse the steps in the planning process.
Identify the different types of plans.
business_studies.summary: Planning involves deciding objectives and courses of action in advance. The outline considers its importance and limitations, the steps in the planning process, and single-use and standing plans such as policies, procedures, programmes and budgets.

business_studies.title: Organising
sections: Steps in the Process of Organising
objectives: Explain the concept of organising.
Explain the process of organising.
Describe the importance of organising.
Explain the meaning, advantages and disadvantages of functional organisation.
Explain the meaning, advantages and disadvantages of divisional organisation.
Explain the meaning, advantages and disadvantages of formal and informal organisation.
Distinguish between formal and informal organisation.
Explain the concept of delegation and decentralisation.
Describe the importance of delegation and decentralisation.
Distinguish between delegation and decentralisation.
business_studies.summary: Organising groups activities and establishes working relationships. The outline covers its process and importance, functional and divisional structures, formal and informal organisation, and the concepts, importance and differences of delegation and decentralisation.

business_studies.title: Staffing
objectives: define staffing.
establish its relationship with Human Resource Management.
state the need and importance of staffing.
describe the steps in the staffing process.
state the meaning of recruitment and selection.
identify important sources of recruitment.
describe the steps in the selection process.
appreciate the need of training and development.
explain various on the job and off the job methods of training.
business_studies.summary: Staffing fills and maintains positions in an organisation. The outline follows staffing as part of human resource management, recruitment and selection, and the importance of training and development, including on-the-job and off-the-job methods.

business_studies.title: Directing
objectives: Explain the concept of directing and its importance in business organisations.
Explain the meaning of motivation and its importance in business management.
Understand and explain Maslow’s theory of hierarchy of needs and its application to motivation of employees in an organisation.
Explain the financial and non-financial incentives through which managers motivate their employees.
Explain the concept of leadership and its importance in management.
Explain about formal and informal communications in the organisations.
Identify various barriers to effective communications and measures to overcome these barriers in the organisations.
business_studies.summary: Directing guides people towards organisational goals. Its elements include supervision, motivation, leadership and communication. The outline considers incentives, hierarchy of needs, leadership, communication channels and barriers to effective communication.

business_studies.title: Controlling
objectives: Explain the meaning of controlling.
State the importance of controlling.
Describe the relationship between planning and controlling.
Explain the steps in the process of controlling.
business_studies.summary: Controlling compares actual performance with planned standards and supports corrective action. The outline considers its importance, relationship with planning and the steps in the control process.

business_studies.title: Financial Management
sections: Factors Affecting the Working Capital Requirements
objectives: explain the meaning of business finance.
describe financial management.
explain the role of financial management in our enterprise.
discuss objectives of financial management and how they could be achieved.
explain the meaning and importance of financial planning.
state the meaning of capital structure.
analyse the factors affecting the choice of an appropriate capital structure.
state meaning of fixed capital and working capital.
analyse the factors affecting the requirement of fixed and working capital.
business_studies.summary: Financial management concerns the procurement and use of funds. The outline covers investment, financing and dividend decisions, financial planning, capital structure and factors influencing fixed and working capital requirements.

business_studies.title: Financial Markets
sections: Capital market: primary and secondary markets
Stock exchange: functions and trading procedure
objectives: Explain financial, money and capital markets and distinguish money and capital markets.
Distinguish primary and secondary capital markets.
Describe stock exchange functions and trading procedure, including depository services and demat accounts.
State the objectives and functions of SEBI.
business_studies.summary: Financial markets connect financial transactions with institutions and participants. This syllabus outline covers money and capital markets, primary and secondary markets, stock exchanges and trading, depository services and the objectives and functions of SEBI.
business_studies.source: CBSE Class 12 Business Studies syllabus 2026–27, unit 10

business_studies.title: Marketing
objectives: explain the meaning of ‘marketing’.
list out important functions of marketing.
explain the elements of marketing-mix.
analyse the factors affecting price of a product.
list out the types of channels of distribution.
explain the major tools of promotion, viz. advertising, personal selling, sales promotion and publicity.
business_studies.summary: Marketing connects organisations with customers through activities and choices about products and markets. The outline covers marketing functions and philosophies and the product, price, physical distribution and promotion elements of the marketing mix.

business_studies.title: Consumer Protection
sections: Ways and Means of Consumer Protection
Redressal Agencies Under the Consumer Protection Act
objectives: Explain the concept and importance of consumer protection.
Describe consumer rights and responsibilities under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.
Identify who can complain, the redressal machinery and remedies.
Describe the role of consumer organisations and NGOs.
business_studies.summary: Consumer protection concerns consumers’ interests and awareness. This outline follows the Consumer Protection Act, 2019: consumers’ rights and responsibilities, complaints, redressal and remedies, and the role of consumer organisations and NGOs.

chemistry.title: Solutions
objectives: Express solution concentration in different units.
Explain Henry’s law, Raoult’s law and deviations from ideal behaviour.
Relate colligative properties to molar mass and abnormal molecular mass.
chemistry.summary: Solutions are classified by their components and described using concentration measures. Solubility, vapour pressure and ideal behaviour lead to colligative properties, which help determine molar mass; association or dissociation can cause abnormal results.
chemistry.figure: Effect of pressure on gas solubility

chemistry.title: Electrochemistry
objectives: Distinguish galvanic and electrolytic cells.
Apply the Nernst equation and relate cell potential to Gibbs energy.
Explain conductance, electrolysis, batteries, fuel cells and corrosion.
chemistry.summary: Electrochemical cells connect chemical reactions with electrical energy. Cell potentials and the Nernst equation describe galvanic cells; conductance, electrolysis, batteries, fuel cells and corrosion connect electrical measurements with chemical change.

chemistry.title: Chemical Kinetics
objectives: Distinguish average and instantaneous reaction rates.
Explain rate laws, order and molecularity and factors affecting rate.
Use zero- and first-order integrated equations and describe temperature dependence and collision theory.
chemistry.summary: Chemical kinetics examines reaction rates and the factors that affect them. Rate laws, order and molecularity describe reactions; integrated equations for zero and first order and the Arrhenius relationship help explain how concentration and temperature influence rates.
chemistry.figure: Instantaneous and average rates of a reaction

chemistry.title: The d- and f-Block Elements
sections: Applications of d- and f-block elements
objectives: Locate d- and f-block elements and describe their electronic configurations.
Discuss trends and properties of transition elements and important compounds.
Compare lanthanoids and actinoids and identify applications.
chemistry.summary: The d- and f-block elements occupy distinct regions of the periodic table. Their electronic configurations help explain trends in transition-metal properties. The unit also considers important compounds, lanthanoids and actinoids, and applications of these elements.
chemistry.figure: Trends in melting points of transition elements

chemistry.title: Coordination Compounds
objectives: Describe Werner’s theory and define coordination terms.
Name mononuclear coordination compounds and identify isomerism.
Explain bonding and describe applications of coordination compounds.
chemistry.summary: Coordination compounds contain a central metal atom or ion surrounded by ligands. The outline covers Werner’s theory, terminology and nomenclature, isomerism and bonding, including metal carbonyls, and applications in chemistry and biological systems.

chemistry.title: Haloalkanes and Haloarenes
objectives: Classify and name haloalkanes and haloarenes.
Describe the nature of the carbon–halogen bond and methods of preparation.
Discuss physical properties, chemical reactions and selected polyhalogen compounds.
chemistry.summary: Haloalkanes and haloarenes contain carbon–halogen bonds in different environments. This outline covers their classification, naming and preparation, the nature of their bonds, physical properties and chemical reactions, and selected polyhalogen compounds.
chemistry.figure: Boiling points of some alkyl halides

chemistry.title: Alcohols, Phenols and Ethers
objectives: Classify and name alcohols, phenols and ethers.
Relate functional-group structures to physical properties.
Describe preparation and chemical reactions of these compounds.
chemistry.summary: Alcohols, phenols and ethers are distinguished by the environments of oxygen-containing functional groups. The outline considers classification, nomenclature and structure, preparation and reactions, physical properties and commercially important alcohols.
chemistry.figure: Structures of methanol, phenol and methoxymethane

chemistry.title: Aldehydes, Ketones and Carboxylic Acids
sections: Nomenclature and structure of the carbonyl group
Properties and reactions of aldehydes and ketones
Nomenclature and structure of the carboxyl group
Properties, reactions and uses of carboxylic acids
objectives: Name and recognise carbonyl and carboxyl compounds.
Describe preparations and reactions of aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids.
Relate structures to properties and discuss acidity and uses.
chemistry.summary: Aldehydes and ketones contain carbonyl groups, while carboxylic acids contain carboxyl groups. The outline covers their nomenclature, structure, preparation, physical properties, characteristic reactions and uses, including factors influencing acid strength.
chemistry.figure: Orbital diagram for the formation of the carbonyl group

chemistry.title: Amines
sections: Preparation and reactions of diazonium salts
Importance of diazonium salts in synthesis
objectives: Classify and name amines and describe their structure.
Discuss preparation, physical properties and chemical reactions of amines.
Describe preparation and reactions of diazonium salts and their importance in synthesis.
chemistry.summary: Amines are nitrogen-containing compounds classified by the groups attached to nitrogen. The outline covers their structure, nomenclature, preparation, properties and reactions, as well as diazonium salts and their importance in aromatic synthesis.

chemistry.title: Biomolecules
objectives: Classify carbohydrates, proteins, vitamins and nucleic acids.
Describe the structures and roles of major biomolecules.
Distinguish DNA and RNA and recognise the roles of enzymes and hormones.
chemistry.summary: Biomolecules support the structure and functions of living systems. This outline introduces carbohydrates, proteins, enzymes, vitamins, nucleic acids and hormones, with attention to classification, molecular structures and the distinction between DNA and RNA.
chemistry.figure: Structure of a nucleoside and a nucleotide

biology.title: Sexual Reproduction in Flowering Plants
biology.summary: Flowers carry the reproductive structures of angiosperms. The chapter follows microsporogenesis and megasporogenesis through pollination into double fertilisation, endosperm and embryo development, and ends with seeds, fruits and apomixis.
sections: Flower structure and the reproductive whorls
objectives: Describe the structure of the anther, ovule and mature embryo sac.
Trace pollination through double fertilisation to seed and fruit formation.
Explain outbreeding devices, parthenocarpy, apomixis and polyembryony with examples.

biology.title: Human Reproduction
biology.summary: Human reproduction runs from the male and female reproductive systems through gametogenesis and the menstrual cycle to fertilisation, implantation and pregnancy, ending with parturition and lactation under hormonal control.
objectives: Explain spermatogenesis and oogenesis with their hormonal control.
Describe the menstrual cycle, fertilisation, cleavage and implantation.
Outline placenta formation, pregnancy, parturition and lactation.

biology.title: Reproductive Health
biology.summary: Reproductive health connects personal well-being with population and society. The chapter covers family planning methods, protection from sexually transmitted infections, infertility and assisted reproductive technologies.
sections: Reproductive health as a social goal
objectives: Compare contraceptive methods by mode of action, effectiveness and side effects.
Identify sexually transmitted infections and describe their prevention.
Explain IVF, ZIFT, GIFT and surrogacy as responses to infertility.

biology.title: Principles of Inheritance and Variation
biology.summary: Mendel's experiments establish the rules of inheritance. The chapter extends them to incomplete dominance, multiple alleles, pleiotropy and linkage, then uses chromosome behaviour to explain sex determination and genetic disorders.
sections: Inheritance of one and two genes
Multiple alleles and the ABO blood group
objectives: Apply Mendel's laws to monohybrid, dihybrid and test crosses.
Explain deviations such as incomplete dominance, codominance, multiple alleles and pleiotropy.
Relate sex determination, linkage and chromosomal disorders to pedigree and karyotype evidence.

biology.title: Molecular Basis of Inheritance
biology.summary: DNA carries heredity. The chapter follows its structure, packaging and semi-conservative replication, then transcription, the genetic code and translation, and closes with gene regulation, the human genome project and DNA fingerprinting.
objectives: Describe the experiments that established DNA as the genetic material.
Explain replication, transcription, the genetic code and translation.
Explain lac operon regulation and the use of DNA fingerprinting.

biology.title: Evolution
biology.summary: Evolution explains the diversity of life as descent with modification. The chapter sets out the evidence, Darwinian natural selection, the Hardy-Weinberg principle, adaptive radiation and the broad pattern of human evolution.
sections: Mechanism of evolution and Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium
objectives: Interpret palaeontological, anatomical and molecular evidence for evolution.
Apply the Hardy-Weinberg principle to allele and genotype frequencies.
Explain natural selection, adaptive radiation, genetic drift and human evolution.

biology.title: Human Health and Disease
biology.summary: Health is more than the absence of disease. The chapter treats pathogens and the immune response, then allergy, autoimmunity, AIDS and cancer, and ends with substance abuse and its prevention.
objectives: Classify pathogens and describe common diseases with their symptoms and vectors.
Explain innate and acquired immunity, including antibody structure.
Describe AIDS, cancer, and the effects and prevention of drug and alcohol abuse.

biology.title: Microbes in Human Welfare
biology.summary: Microbes work across food, industry and medicine. The chapter covers fermentation, antibiotics, sewage treatment, biogas, biocontrol agents and biofertilisers, alongside the diseases some of them cause.
objectives: Describe the role of microbes in fermented foods and industrial products.
Explain sewage treatment and biogas generation.
Explain biocontrol agents and biofertilisers as alternatives to chemicals.

biology.title: Biotechnology: Principles and Processes
biology.summary: Biotechnology joins living systems to technology. The chapter covers restriction enzymes, cloning vectors and recombinant DNA construction, then PCR and gel electrophoresis, bioreactors and downstream processing.
objectives: Explain the role of restriction enzymes, vectors and competent hosts.
Describe the steps from DNA isolation to selection of recombinants.
Explain PCR, gel electrophoresis, bioreactor operation and downstream processing.

biology.title: Biotechnology and its Applications
biology.summary: Recombinant DNA reaches agriculture, medicine and industry. The chapter covers Bt crops and RNA interference, recombinant insulin, gene therapy, molecular diagnosis, transgenic animals and the ethics of biopiracy.
objectives: Explain how Bt toxin genes and RNA interference protect crops.
Describe recombinant insulin and gene therapy for ADA deficiency.
Explain molecular diagnosis and the ethical issues around patenting living material.

biology.title: Organisms and Populations
biology.summary: Ecology starts with the organism and its adaptations, then scales up to populations: density, exponential and logistic growth, life-history variation and the interactions between species.
objectives: Relate adaptations to temperature, water, light and soil conditions.
Apply the exponential and logistic growth equations and define carrying capacity.
Classify population interactions with examples.

biology.title: Ecosystem
biology.summary: An ecosystem couples organisms with their physical surroundings through energy flow and nutrient cycling. The chapter covers productivity, decomposition, food chains, ecological pyramids and succession.
objectives: Distinguish gross and net primary productivity and explain decomposition.
Trace energy flow through trophic levels and interpret ecological pyramids.
Describe succession and the cycling of carbon, nitrogen and phosphorus.

biology.title: Biodiversity and Conservation
biology.summary: Biodiversity is the variety of life at genetic, species and ecosystem level. The chapter covers how it is measured, why it matters, its patterns and losses, and the in-situ and ex-situ strategies used to conserve it.
objectives: Describe the levels and patterns of biodiversity, including species-area relationships.
Explain the causes of biodiversity loss and the idea of extinction debt.
Compare in-situ and ex-situ conservation with Indian examples.
